Issue #72 (HHH-21191): easy-call for a narrowly scoped nullable self-reference fix, subject to reproducing the reported H2 failure. Sole issue in verified batch, no duplicate. Two-way: Hibernate Core delete planning only, no public API or persisted schema change proposed.

Static source at the pinned head: DeleteCoordinatorStandard and DeleteDecomposerStandard visit mutable tables in reverse order and skip only mappings marked cascade-delete-enabled. The root-table association FK is distinct from the subclass primary-key FK back to the root. DefaultDeleteEventListener calls ForeignKeys.Nullifier for the legacy path; self-reference nullification is currently dialect-workaround-gated. Related HHH-21133 preserves the MySQL/MariaDB nullable-reference workaround and does not verify H2. Investigate reusing a narrowly selected nullable-reference break in both paths; do not globally reorder deletes or change dialect support flags. Non-nullable cyclic relationships are out of this scope.

First run the public Jira fixture on unchanged pinned production code; require the reported 23503 at subclass deletion, not a fixture skip or setup failure. Then assert that both physical rows are gone after commit, exercise legacy and graph queues, and preserve adjacent MySQL/MariaDB controls. Check PostgreSQL via Hibernate if shared deletion logic changes. No test was run in Explore and no change was made.
